evidence: The pinned script documents empty/truncated checksum responses and requires a nonempty well-formed SHA256 record before invoking the platform checksum utility; README and release docs distinguish integrity-only checking from authenticity.
adoption.rationale: A malformed HTTP response or empty checksum file must not be accepted as an integrity result merely because an installed checksum utility ignores malformed/empty input. The source preflight is the shared fail-closed guard; this contract makes no authenticity claim.

declared_domain: One ASCII LF-delimited checksum or error-response line, excluding NUL; the solver property covers every line of length 0..63, with no additional content assumptions. The product gate exercises the pinned verifier with an empty file, a longer checksum-free response, and a well-formed checksum record. The guarantee is only that no source-pattern match occurs without the required 64-hex prefix and delimiters; the solver does not prove authenticity or the external checksum utility's behavior.
guarantee: When a downloaded SHA256SUMS file has no line beginning with exactly 64 ASCII hexadecimal digits followed by POSIX whitespace, an optional '*' marker, and a non-whitespace filename character, verify-release.sh fails before calling the platform checksum command and cannot print an integrity success result. This is a preflight guarantee only; it does not establish release authenticity.
input_source: The SHA256SUMS text file supplied alongside a downloaded release artifact; until signature verification succeeds, its bytes are untrusted network input. The helper also documents integrity-only mode while the maintainer signing key is unavailable.
